Subject: POC follow-up: prompt set & eval plan

Hi Alex / Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC started smoothly: 

Recap / success criteria (from our conversation)
- Evaluate Redwood inference on ACME’s customer-support summarization flow (500–1,000 session samples)
- Qualitative: summary usefulness score >= 4/5 on internal rubric
- Quantitative: ROUGE-L/Recall baseline improvement vs current transformer model; target +8–12% on sample set
- Latency: p50 < 200ms for generation on Dedicated profile; p95 < 500ms
- Cost: comparable or lower token spend than current endpoint (we’ll report cost per 1k tokens at trial)

What we need from ACME to run the eval
- Prompt set: CSV or JSONL with columns: prompt_id, user_message, convo_context (optional), expected_label/summary (if available), priority_tag, redaction_flag
- Logs: anonymized examples of raw user messages where possible (we can accept redacted/pseudonymized versions)
- Ownership: who at ACME will own prompt collation and sign-off (you mentioned Sara?)

Proposed timeline
- 2026-06-22: ACME provides prompt set + any sample logs (target 200–500 prompts to start)
- 2026-06-24 to 2026-06-26: Redwood builds eval harness & runs first pass (Aditya owning engineering work)
- 2026-06-29: First results deck + quality review meeting (Monica + Marissa to lead)

Attachments & templates
- I attached a lightweight prompt_collection_template.csv and we also put a sample in the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/abc123

Quick asks for you today
1) Confirm Sara (or other owner) will share the prompt set by 2026-06-22
2) Confirm whether prompts will include expected labels/summaries or we should expect to label on Redwood side
3) Any constraints around PII/redaction that we should follow (we have redaction guidance we can share)

If that all looks good I’ll block time with Aditya and Monica and send a calendar invite for the first results review.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Alex — perfect, thanks for the sample. That layout looks fine; the template should be compatible. Answers to your clarifying Qs below and a bit more detail on how we’ll run the eval: 

PII & redaction
- Preferred pattern: replace emails/phones/names with tokens like [REDACTED_EMAIL], [REDACTED_PHONE], [REDACTED_NAME]. If you prefer handing us a script we can provide a small Python snippet for deterministic redaction.
- If any records are regulated data (health/PHI, financial), please mark them and we’ll keep them out of any shared internal benchmark datasets; we can run isolated evals in Private deployment if needed.

Evaluation plan (high level) — Aditya/Redwood engineering to implement: 
1) Ingest prompt CSV/JSONL and normalize fields (prompt_id, user_message, context, expected_label)
2) Run generation sweep across 3 model variants + quantization profiles (hosted/dedicated-compatible)
3) Compute automated metrics (ROUGE, exact match, token counts, latency distributions)
4) Sample 50 outputs per model for manual quality scoring (use ACME rubric)
5) Deliver results deck and suggested tuning (prompt tweaks, model variant, batching/quantization settings)

Primary owners
- ACME: Sara Lee (prompt collection & label sign-off)
- Redwood: Aditya Rao (eval pipeline), Monica Patel (quality review & success criteria owner), Marissa Cole (commercial lead)

Proposed timeline (updated)
- 2026-06-22: ACME delivers prompts + any labeled summaries
- 2026-06-24: Redwood runs first sweep and shares preliminary metrics
- 2026-06-29: Results review + decision on next steps

If that aligns, we’ll treat 2026-06-22 as the delivery milestone and move forward. I’ll attach our redaction snippet and the prompt template again.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marissa Cole
